_meta.scale_notes: vad values on 1-10 scale: valence 1=very negative/10=very positive, arousal 1=calm/10=intense, dominance 1=powerless/10=in control. Verse IDs reference the canonical verse pool established across Documents 1, 3, and the build plan.

emotions.name: Acute Grief
what_people_say: I lost someone and I don't know how to exist without them
Everything reminds me of them
I can't stop crying
It doesn't feel real yet
I keep reaching for my phone to call them
emotions.hidden_beneath: fear that the love itself has ended, not just the person

patterns: past tense mixed with present
third person about the deceased
fragmented, incomplete sentences

emotions.likely_defence: denial or duty-armor (staying strong for others)
emotions.south_asian_expression: often mixed with duty language — 'I have to be strong for the family.' Direct grief expression suppressed, especially for men.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह पीड़ा भारी है। जो तुमने खोया है, वह शब्दों में नहीं समाता।
pre_validation_line.en: This pain is heavy. What you've lost doesn't fit into words.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.2 - changing worn clothes for new

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: अभी तुम्हारे साथ कौन है?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Who is with you right now?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never rebuke. Never rush to teaching before presence has been established. Never say 'they are in a better place' — this is not Krishna's register.

emotions.name: Complicated Grief
what_people_say: It's been a year, I should be over this by now
Why am I still like this
Everyone else has moved on
I feel guilty for still grieving
I don't want to burden people with this again
emotions.hidden_beneath: shame about the grief itself, layered on top of the original loss

patterns: self-criticism embedded in grief language
comparison to imagined others' timelines

emotions.likely_defence: minimisation
emotions.south_asian_expression: grief given a time limit by family expectation — 'chalta hai, life goes on' used to shut down continued mourning.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम्हें दुख नहीं, दुख होने पर शर्म आ रही है।
pre_validation_line.en: It's not the grief troubling you most right now. It's feeling ashamed that you're still grieving.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.10 - timing, nothing blooms before its season

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: किसने तुम्हें बताया कि दुख का समय निश्चित होता है?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Who decided grief has a deadline?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never validate the 'should be over it' framing, even implicitly.

emotions.name: Anticipatory Grief
what_people_say: I'm scared of losing them
Every visit feels like it could be the last
I can't enjoy time with them because I'm already mourning
I don't know how I'll survive when it happens
I keep preparing for a goodbye that hasn't come yet
emotions.hidden_beneath: grieving in advance as a way to control the pain — rehearsal instead of presence

patterns: future-tense catastrophising
present moment described through a future loss lens

emotions.likely_defence: rehearsal as control (a form of intellectualisation)
emotions.south_asian_expression: common with aging parents abroad — distance intensifies the anticipatory quality; visits become charged with unspoken finality.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम अभी के पल को भी उस दुख से भर रहे हो जो अभी आया ही नहीं।
pre_validation_line.en: You're spending the time you still have grieving a loss that hasn't arrived yet.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.12 - the hourglass, the narrow present

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: जब तुम उनके साथ होते हो, तुम्हारा मन कहां होता है — साथ में, या पहले से हुए बिछड़ने में?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: When you're actually with them, where is your mind — present, or already at the goodbye?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never confirm the fear as prophecy. Never say 'yes, prepare yourself' — redirect toward presence, not toward more rehearsal.

emotions.name: Disenfranchised Grief
what_people_say: Nobody understands why I'm this sad
It's not like someone died, so I feel stupid grieving
People keep telling me to move on because it wasn't a 'real' loss
I lost something that mattered and no one validates it
I feel embarrassed for how much this is affecting me
emotions.hidden_beneath: the isolation of grieving something the world doesn't recognise as loss-worthy (a career, an identity, a friendship, a version of the future)

patterns: pre-emptive self-invalidation before describing the actual loss

emotions.likely_defence: minimisation
emotions.south_asian_expression: loss of a career path, a broken engagement, or a rejected dream are often treated by family as embarrassments to move past quickly rather than losses to mourn.

pre_validation_line.hi: जो टूटा है, उसे तुम खुद भी शोक के योग्य नहीं मानते — इसीलिए यह अकेलापन दोगुना है।
pre_validation_line.en: Part of what makes this so heavy is that you don't even feel allowed to call it a loss.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.5 - a few leaves falling, still part of the tree's story

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: अगर किसी और के साथ यह होता, क्या तुम उनके दुख को छोटा मानते?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: If this had happened to someone you loved, would you call their grief small?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never ask 'is it really that serious' framing, even softly.

emotions.name: Regret
what_people_say: I should have done it differently
If only I had chosen the other path
I keep replaying that decision
I can't forgive myself for what I didn't do
It's too late now anyway
emotions.hidden_beneath: belief that the past self should have known what only the present self now knows

patterns: conditional past tense (would have/could have)
replaying/looping language

emotions.likely_defence: rumination as false control
emotions.south_asian_expression: often tied to career or marriage path decisions weighed against family expectation — regret framed as having disappointed others, not just self.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम आज के ज्ञान से बीते हुए स्वयं को दोष दे रहे हो।
pre_validation_line.en: You're judging who you were then with the knowledge you only have now.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.5 - leaves falling, part of the tree's continuing life

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: उस समय, जो जानकारी तुम्हारे पास थी, उसके साथ यह निर्णय कितना अनुचित था?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: With what you actually knew at the time, how unreasonable was that decision, really?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never say 'everything happens for a reason' — the Gita does not teach this; it teaches responsibility without permanent self-punishment.

emotions.name: Fear of Failure
what_people_say: What if I'm not good enough
I can't stop thinking about what happens if this doesn't work
My whole future feels like it depends on this one thing
I'd rather not try than try and fail publicly
Everyone is watching and waiting for me to mess up
emotions.hidden_beneath: identity fused with outcome — belief that failing at the task means failing as a person

patterns: catastrophising future scenarios
conflating action with identity ('if I fail' becomes 'if I am a failure')

emotions.likely_defence: avoidance disguised as pragmatism
emotions.south_asian_expression: family investment framing — 'my parents sacrificed for this' turns personal failure into a feared betrayal of others.

pre_validation_line.hi: डर परिणाम का नहीं — डर यह है कि हारने पर तुम खुद क्या मान बैठोगे।
pre_validation_line.en: This isn't really fear of the outcome. It's fear of what you'll believe about yourself if it goes wrong.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.1 - the closed fist versus the open palm

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: अगर यह असफल हो, तो सबसे भारी बात क्या होगी — नतीजा, या उसका तुम्हारे बारे में क्या मतलब निकलेगा?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: If this fails, what's actually the heaviest part — the outcome, or what it would mean about you?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never say 'you won't fail' — a false promise. Reframe the relationship to outcome, don't deny the possibility.

emotions.name: Anxiety About the Future
what_people_say: I can't stop worrying about what's coming
My mind won't settle down
I feel like something bad is about to happen
I keep planning for every possible outcome and it's exhausting
I can't be present, I'm always three steps ahead in my head
emotions.hidden_beneath: an attempt to control an uncontrollable future through mental rehearsal

patterns: future tense dominance
run-on sentence structure mirroring racing thoughts

emotions.likely_defence: hypervigilance as false safety
emotions.south_asian_expression: tied closely to family financial or visa/status anxiety in diaspora contexts — worry as a form of duty rather than a symptom.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम्हारा मन भविष्य को नियंत्रित करने की कोशिश कर रहा है — इसीलिए वह टिक नहीं पाता।
pre_validation_line.en: Your mind is trying to control a future it can't actually reach yet. That's why it can't rest.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.12 - the hourglass, only the present is actually yours

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: अभी, इसी क्षण में, वह डर सच हो रहा है, या सिर्फ सोचा जा रहा है?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Right now, in this exact moment, is the feared thing actually happening, or only being imagined?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never say 'don't worry' — that dismisses rather than redirects. Give the mind somewhere real to return to.

emotions.name: Fear of Judgment (Log Kya Kahenge)
what_people_say: What will people think if I do this
I can't get past what my family will say
I keep choosing what looks right over what feels right
I'm scared of the gossip
My decisions aren't really mine, they're everyone else's opinions
emotions.hidden_beneath: identity built on external validation rather than internal conviction

patterns: decisions described through others' anticipated reactions rather than own preference

emotions.likely_defence: people-pleasing as identity protection
emotions.south_asian_expression: central to South Asian social fabric — this is not vanity, it is genuine fear of social/familial exile. Take it seriously rather than dismissing it as shallow.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह डर उनके शब्दों का नहीं — यह डर है कि तुम्हारी अपनी आवाज़ पर्याप्त नहीं।
pre_validation_line.en: This fear isn't really about their words. It's about whether your own voice is enough on its own.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.6 - the chain you're bound to shapes what you become

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: अगर कोई तुम्हारा निर्णय कभी नहीं जानता, तो तुम क्या चुनते?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: If no one would ever find out what you chose, what would you choose?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never dismiss the social stakes as trivial — for this audience, they are genuinely high. Take the fear seriously before reframing it.

emotions.name: Fear of Death / Impermanence
what_people_say: I think about dying sometimes and it terrifies me
Everything feels so temporary
I don't know how to make peace with not existing
I'm scared of losing everyone I love, eventually
What's the point if it all ends anyway
emotions.hidden_beneath: a confrontation with impermanence that the mind has no framework to hold

patterns: universal/existential framing rather than a specific triggering event

emotions.likely_defence: avoidance of the topic entirely, or intellectualisation about death philosophically
emotions.south_asian_expression: often surfaces around a family member's illness or aging parents, layered with distance-guilt for those living abroad.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह डर मृत्यु का नहीं — यह डर है कि जो तुम प्रेम करते हो, वह खो जाएगा।
pre_validation_line.en: This isn't really fear of death. It's fear of everything you love slipping away.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.8 - a drop of water becoming the ocean

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: जब यह विचार आता है, वह किस समय आता है — रात में, या जब तुम किसी को बहुत प्रेम करते हुए महसूस करते हो?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: When this thought comes, when does it usually arrive — at night, or when you're feeling especially close to someone?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never offer religious platitudes as a substitute for the actual teaching on the eternal self — go to the real philosophy, not a comforting cliché.

emotions.name: Existential Dread
what_people_say: None of this feels like it matters
I don't know why I'm even doing any of this
What's the actual point of any of it
I feel like I'm just going through motions that lead nowhere
Even my achievements feel hollow
emotions.hidden_beneath: a genuine, serious confrontation with meaning — not laziness, not depression necessarily, but a real philosophical crisis

patterns: universal, abstract framing
often follows an achievement, not a failure

emotions.likely_defence: intellectualisation of the crisis to avoid feeling its full weight
emotions.south_asian_expression: frequently hits high achievers who have fulfilled every external family/cultural expectation and find no relief on the other side.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह खालीपन असफलता से नहीं आया — यह तब आता है जब मिल जाने के बाद भी कुछ अधूरा लगे।
pre_validation_line.en: This emptiness didn't come from failing. It came from arriving somewhere and finding it wasn't what you thought it would be.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.8 - a drop merging into the ocean, not disappearing but expanding

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: यह भाव कब से है — किसी असफलता के बाद, या किसी सफलता के बाद?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: When did this actually start — after something went wrong, or after something went right?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never treat this as depression requiring reassurance — it is often a genuine philosophical crisis and deserves real philosophical engagement, not deflection.

emotions.name: Acute Anger / Rage
what_people_say: I'm so angry I can't think straight
I want to say things I know I'll regret
They had no right to do that
I can't let this go
I feel like I could explode
emotions.hidden_beneath: almost always fear or grief that anger is protecting — powerlessness converted into heat

patterns: short, forceful sentences
high exclamation density
blame-focused subject-verb structure

emotions.likely_defence: displacement (anger easier to feel than the vulnerability underneath)
emotions.south_asian_expression: anger toward family is often redirected elsewhere (work, strangers, self) because direct expression toward elders is culturally suppressed.

pre_validation_line.hi: क्रोध के नीचे कुछ और है — डर, या चोट।
pre_validation_line.en: Underneath the anger, there's usually something quieter — fear, or hurt.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.7 - the cascade from desire to anger to collapse

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: अगर यह गुस्सा बोल सकता, तो वह क्या मांग रहा होता?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: If this anger could speak plainly, what would it actually be asking for?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never rebuke on the first disclosure of fresh anger. Rebuke is only appropriate later, if the anger is being used to justify ongoing self-destructive avoidance.

emotions.name: Chronic Resentment
what_people_say: I gave everything and got nothing back
It's not fair how much I've done for them
I keep score even though I don't want to
I smile but I'm keeping a mental list
I don't think I can ever fully forgive this
emotions.hidden_beneath: unexpressed grief over an imbalance never acknowledged by the other party

patterns: accounting language — ledger, debt, owed

emotions.likely_defence: rationalisation of continued self-sacrifice as virtue
emotions.south_asian_expression: extremely common in eldest-child and caregiver dynamics; resentment toward parents or siblings is one of the most suppressed emotions culturally.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह गुस्सा नहीं है जितना यह थकान है — कभी न पहचाने गए त्याग की थकान।
pre_validation_line.en: This is less anger, more exhaustion — the exhaustion of giving something that was never truly seen.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.6 - what you bind yourself to shapes what you become

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: अगर वे आज माफी मांग लें, क्या यह भार हट जाएगा?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: If they apologised today, would the weight actually lift?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never rush to 'forgive them' language — resentment needs to be named and understood before release is even relevant.

emotions.name: Frustration
what_people_say: Nothing I do seems to work
I'm putting in so much effort for so little result
I keep hitting the same wall
I don't know why this is so hard
I feel like giving up on this specific thing, not everything
emotions.hidden_beneath: effort disconnected from visible outcome, threatening the belief that effort matters at all

patterns: repetition of failed-attempt language
narrower scope than general hopelessness — targeted at one domain

emotions.likely_defence: none typically — usually genuine, direct frustration
emotions.south_asian_expression: often tied to visible comparison — siblings or peers achieving the same goal with apparently less struggle.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम्हें रुकना नहीं है — तुम्हें बस यह स्वीकारना है कि परिणाम कब आएगा, यह तुम्हारे हाथ में कभी नहीं था।
pre_validation_line.en: You don't actually want to quit. You want the effort to guarantee the result — and it never did.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.10 - flowers don't bloom before their season

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: क्या तुम्हारा असंतोष प्रयास से है, या नतीजे से?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Is the frustration with the effort itself, or with the result you haven't gotten yet?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never suggest quitting is the answer, and never suggest 'just try harder' — both dismiss the real appraisal problem.

emotions.name: Envy
what_people_say: Why does everyone else have it figured out
I hate that I feel this way about my friend's success
I compare myself constantly and it's exhausting
Their life looks so much easier than mine
I feel ashamed for being jealous of someone I care about
emotions.hidden_beneath: a private fear of being left behind, often layered with guilt about the envy itself

patterns: comparison structure — 'they have X, I have Y'
self-condemnation for the feeling itself

emotions.likely_defence: self-punishment (shaming oneself for the envy rather than examining it)
emotions.south_asian_expression: amplified by direct family/community comparison culture — envy toward cousins or peers carries extra shame because comparison itself is normalised, making the feeling paradoxically more secret.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह ईर्ष्या नहीं जितना यह डर है — पीछे छूट जाने का डर।
pre_validation_line.en: This is less envy, more fear — the fear of being left behind.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.6 - the chain you bind yourself to

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: क्या तुम उनकी सफलता चाहते हो, या उनका रास्ता?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Do you actually want their outcome, or their exact path?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never shame the person further for feeling envy — that just doubles the pattern.

emotions.name: Anger From Betrayal
what_people_say: I trusted them completely and they did this
How could someone I loved do this to me
I don't know how to trust anyone now
Everything I believed about them was a lie
I want them to feel what I'm feeling
emotions.hidden_beneath: grief for the relationship as it was believed to be, not just anger at the act

patterns: before/after framing — 'I used to think... now I know'

emotions.likely_defence: vengeance fantasy as displaced grief processing
emotions.south_asian_expression: betrayal by family (not just romantic partners) carries extra weight given collectivist trust structures — family betrayal often goes unspoken for years.

pre_validation_line.hi: गुस्सा उनके किए हुए का नहीं है उतना — यह उस रिश्ते के लिए शोक है जो तुमने सच माना था।
pre_validation_line.en: This anger isn't only about what they did. It's grief for the relationship you believed you had.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.6 - what you bind yourself to shapes what you become

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: इस समय, तुम्हें उनसे क्या चाहिए — जवाब, माफी, या सिर्फ यह स्वीकार करना कि यह हुआ?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Right now, what do you actually need from them — an explanation, an apology, or just acknowledgment that it happened?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never rush toward forgiveness. Never say 'let it go' before the grief underneath has been named.

emotions.name: Core Shame
what_people_say: I'm fundamentally broken
There's something wrong with me
I don't deserve good things
If people really knew me they'd leave
I am the problem
emotions.hidden_beneath: global self-condemnation — this is about identity ('I am'), not behaviour ('I did')

patterns: identity-level statements rather than behaviour-level ones — the critical shame vs guilt distinction

emotions.likely_defence: self-attack as a form of pre-emptive control (attacking self before others can)
emotions.south_asian_expression: often rooted in comparison to siblings/cousins or perceived family disappointment; shame is frequently inherited language, not self-generated.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम अपने किए हुए की बात नहीं कर रहे — तुम अपने होने की बात कर रहे हो। ये दो अलग चीज़ें हैं।
pre_validation_line.en: You're not describing something you did. You're describing who you believe you are. Those are not the same thing.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.1 - the closed fist versus the open palm

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: क्या यह भाव किसी घटना के बाद आया, या यह हमेशा से था, पीछे कहीं?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Did this feeling come from something specific, or has it always been there, underneath everything?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never argue directly against the shame ('that's not true'). Instead, gently expose the identity-vs-behaviour confusion.

emotions.name: Specific Guilt
what_people_say: I did something terrible
I can't stop thinking about what I did
I hurt someone and I don't know how to make it right
I feel like I need to be punished
I keep apologising even when they've moved on
emotions.hidden_beneath: a real moral event that needs acknowledgment, repair where possible, and release — not endless self-punishment

patterns: specific, behaviour-level language (contrast with shame_core's identity-level language)

emotions.likely_defence: self-punishment as substitute for actual repair
emotions.south_asian_expression: guilt toward parents specifically (disappointing them, not fulfilling duty) is often more acute than guilt toward peers.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम जो हुआ उसे ठीक करना चाहते हो — पर तुम खुद को दंड देकर उसे ठीक करने की कोशिश कर रहे हो।
pre_validation_line.en: You want to make this right. But you're trying to make it right by punishing yourself, and those aren't the same thing.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.1 - lotus leaf untouched by water

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: क्या इसे सुधारने का कोई वास्तविक तरीका बचा है, या अब यह सिर्फ भार ढोने की बात है?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Is there an actual way left to repair this, or has this become only about carrying the weight of it?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never minimise real harm done — take genuine wrongdoing seriously while separating the act from total identity.

emotions.name: Unworthiness
what_people_say: I don't deserve good things
I feel like a fraud even when things go well
I sabotage myself right when things start working
I don't think I've earned this
Good things happening make me suspicious, not happy
emotions.hidden_beneath: a belief formed early that worth must be earned continuously, never simply held

patterns: good outcomes described with discomfort rather than relief

emotions.likely_defence: self-sabotage as a way to control the disappointment (better to fail on your own terms)
emotions.south_asian_expression: frequently tied to conditional-love patterns rooted in academic/career achievement culture.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम्हें डर है कि यह अच्छाई छिन जाएगी — इसलिए तुम खुद उसे पहले छोड़ देना चाहते हो।
pre_validation_line.en: You're afraid this good thing will be taken away — so part of you wants to let it go first, on your own terms.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.11 - coal becoming diamond through time and pressure

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: कब से लगता है कि अच्छा होने के लिए तुम्हें उसे लगातार कमाना पड़ता है?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Since when has it felt like goodness has to be constantly re-earned, never just held?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never simply say 'you deserve good things' as a bare assertion — it will bounce off. Trace the belief to its root instead.

emotions.name: Imposter Syndrome
what_people_say: I feel like I'm going to be found out
Everyone here is smarter than me
I got lucky, that's the only reason I'm here
I don't actually belong in this room
One day they'll realise I'm not as good as they think
emotions.hidden_beneath: measuring self against an external standard that was never truly one's own to begin with

patterns: achievement described as accidental, not earned
comparison to a room/group's imagined standard

emotions.likely_defence: attributing success to luck to pre-empt future disappointment
emotions.south_asian_expression: acute in first-generation contexts entering elite institutions or workplaces — belonging feels conditional on constant proof.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम किसी और के मापदंड से खुद को माप रहे हो — जो कभी तुम्हारा अपना मापदंड था ही नहीं।
pre_validation_line.en: You're measuring yourself against a standard that was never actually yours to begin with.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.10 - flowers don't bloom before their season

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: यह जगह किसने बनाई — तुमने, या किसी और की परिभाषा ने?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Who defined what belonging in this room actually looks like — you, or someone else's standard?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never list their achievements back at them as proof — this rarely lands. Address the standard itself, not the evidence against it.

emotions.name: Unresolved Remorse
what_people_say: I can't forgive myself
It's been years and I still think about it
I never got to make it right, they're gone now
I don't think I deserve to feel okay about this
I carry this every single day
emotions.hidden_beneath: a moral debt that feels permanently unpayable, often because the other person is unreachable or gone

patterns: long time-span language ('years', 'every day') marking a chronic, not acute, state

emotions.likely_defence: permanent self-punishment as a substitute for closure that can't be obtained externally
emotions.south_asian_expression: very common with unresolved conflict with a parent who has since passed — the guilt becomes frozen because the relationship can no longer change.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम एक ऐसा भार उठा रहे हो जिसे चुकाने का रास्ता अब बाहर नहीं बचा — इसलिए तुम उसे भीतर ही ढो रहे हो।
pre_validation_line.en: You're carrying a debt that no longer has an outward way to be repaid — so you've been repaying it inward instead, endlessly.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.2 - the soul changes bodies like changing clothes, but love does not end

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: अगर वे आज तुम्हारे सामने होते, वे क्या कहते?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: If they were in front of you today, what do you think they would actually say?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never suggest 'just forgive yourself' as a simple instruction — this is not a switch. Move through surrender (18.66), not through denial of the debt.

emotions.name: Deep Loneliness
what_people_say: Nobody actually understands me
I'm surrounded by people but feel completely alone
I could disappear and nobody would notice
I perform a version of myself for everyone
The real me stays hidden
emotions.hidden_beneath: a longing to be truly known, not merely accompanied

patterns: contrast structure — surrounded by people vs. feeling alone

emotions.likely_defence: performing a social self while withholding the real one
emotions.south_asian_expression: particularly acute in diaspora — surrounded by culture and community that doesn't fully see the individual's specific inner life.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम इतने समय से एक भूमिका निभा रहे हो कि खुद तक वापस जाने का रास्ता भूल गए हो।
pre_validation_line.en: You've been performing a version of yourself for so long that even you have lost the thread back to who's underneath it.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.8 - a drop merging with the ocean, never truly separate

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: आखिरी बार कब किसी ने तुम्हारा असली रूप देखा था, वह रूप जो तुम छुपाते हो?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: When was the last time someone saw the version of you that you keep hidden?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never respond with 'you're not alone, I'm here' as a substitute for real human connection — point back toward it, don't replace it.

emotions.name: Diaspora Isolation
what_people_say: I haven't seen my family in so long
I don't fully belong here, but I don't fully belong back home anymore either
Nobody around me understands where I come from
I'm homesick for a place that doesn't quite exist as I remember it
I'm doing this all alone, far from everyone who actually knows me
emotions.hidden_beneath: grief for a version of belonging that geography has permanently altered, not just distance

patterns: dual-location language — describing displacement from both places at once

emotions.likely_defence: overworking as compensation for the isolation
emotions.south_asian_expression: this is the core condition for a large share of this product's actual users — take with full weight, do not generalise into ordinary homesickness.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम दो जगहों के बीच खड़े हो, और दोनों में से किसी में भी पूरी तरह से नहीं हो — यह अपने आप में एक अकेलापन है।
pre_validation_line.en: You're standing between two places, fully belonging to neither right now — that itself is its own particular kind of lonely.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.9 - a lamp holding against deep darkness

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: इस समय, तुम्हें घर की सबसे ज़्यादा याद किस चीज़ की आती है — किसी व्यक्ति की, या किसी एहसास की?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Right now, what do you miss most about home — a specific person, or a specific feeling?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never suggest 'just go back' or 'just call home more' as a fix — the condition is structural, not solved by a single action.

emotions.name: Fear of Abandonment
what_people_say: Everyone eventually leaves
I'm scared they'll get tired of me
I push people away before they can leave first
I don't trust that people will stay
I feel like I have to earn people staying in my life
emotions.hidden_beneath: an early wound around reliability of care, now generalised to all relationships

patterns: universal predictive language ('everyone', 'always') generalising from specific past experience

emotions.likely_defence: pre-emptive withdrawal (leaving before being left)
emotions.south_asian_expression: can stem from early experiences of being sent abroad for education, or a parent's prolonged absence for work — abandonment doesn't require malice to leave a mark.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम लोगों को पहले ही जाने देने की तैयारी कर लेते हो — ताकि उनका जाना तुम्हारा फैसला लगे, उनका नहीं।
pre_validation_line.en: You get ready for people to leave before they do — so that when it happens, it feels like your choice, not theirs.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.9 - a lamp holding against deep darkness

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: यह विश्वास कब शुरू हुआ कि लोग रुकते नहीं?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: When did the belief that people don't stay actually begin?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never promise permanence you can't guarantee ('I'll never leave you') — this recreates the exact pattern instead of addressing it.

emotions.name: Feeling Invisible
what_people_say: Nobody notices when I'm struggling
I could stop showing up and it would take a while for anyone to realise
I've stopped expecting to be asked how I'm doing
I feel like background noise in my own life
I take care of everyone and no one takes care of me
emotions.hidden_beneath: a role (usually caregiving) that has consumed the person's visibility as an individual with needs

patterns: caregiver-role language embedded within the loneliness description

emotions.likely_defence: over-functioning as a way to remain needed even while feeling unseen
emotions.south_asian_expression: very common for eldest daughters/sons and primary caregivers within family structures — invisibility disguised as duty.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम सबको देखते हो — और खुद को देखे जाने का इंतज़ार करते-करते थक गए हो।
pre_validation_line.en: You see everyone else clearly. You've just gotten tired of waiting to be seen back.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.8 - a drop merging with the ocean, never truly unseen by it

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: आखिरी बार कब किसी ने तुमसे पूछा था कि तुम कैसे हो — और वाकई जवाब का इंतज़ार किया था?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: When did someone last ask how you're doing — and actually wait for the real answer?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never suggest they simply 'ask for help' without acknowledging why that has felt impossible within their role.

emotions.name: Disconnection Amid People
what_people_say: I'm at the party but I feel like I'm watching from outside
I go through conversations on autopilot
I don't feel present even when I'm with close friends
Everyone seems connected except me
I smile and laugh but nothing lands
emotions.hidden_beneath: dissociation from genuine presence, often protective, following accumulated small disappointments in connection

patterns: observer/spectator language — describing one's own life from outside it

emotions.likely_defence: dissociation as protection from repeated micro-disappointments in connection
emotions.south_asian_expression: can occur specifically within large family gatherings — surrounded by relatives yet privately unseen as an individual beyond one's role.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम वहां हो, पर तुम्हारा मन कहीं और खड़ा होकर देख रहा है।
pre_validation_line.en: You're there, but part of you is standing somewhere off to the side, just watching.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.8 - all beings connected through the same underlying presence

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: यह कब से हो रहा है — हमेशा से, या हाल ही में शुरू हुआ?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Has this always been true for you, or did it start more recently?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never suggest they're simply 'not trying hard enough' to connect — this is protective, not lazy.

emotions.name: Lost Sense of Self
what_people_say: I don't know who I am anymore
I used to know what I wanted, now I don't
I feel like I've been playing a role for so long I forgot the real version
Everyone else seems to know themselves, I don't
I don't recognise myself in the mirror sometimes
emotions.hidden_beneath: identity that was built around external roles (student, employee, family position) now destabilised by a change in those roles

patterns: past-versus-present identity contrast

emotions.likely_defence: clinging to an outdated role rather than sitting with the uncertainty of redefinition
emotions.south_asian_expression: commonly triggered by graduation, immigration, or a major life-stage shift where inherited identity markers no longer clearly apply.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुमने जिस भूमिका को अपना माना था, वह बदल गई है — और उसके नीचे जो असली तुम है, वह अभी अनजान लग रहा है।
pre_validation_line.en: The role you thought was you has shifted — and what's underneath it feels unfamiliar right now.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.2 - changing worn clothes, the wearer remains

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: आखिरी बार कब तुम्हें लगा था कि तुम वाकई खुद को जानते हो?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: When was the last time you genuinely felt like you knew yourself?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never hand them a pre-packaged new identity to adopt — the Gita's answer is discovering the constant beneath the changing roles, not replacing one role with another.

emotions.name: Directionless
what_people_say: I don't know what I'm doing with my life
I have no clear path forward
Everyone around me seems to have a plan
I feel like I'm just drifting
I don't know what I actually want
emotions.hidden_beneath: confusion between not having a plan and not having permission to choose one's own

patterns: comparison to others' apparent clarity

emotions.likely_defence: waiting for clarity to arrive before acting, rather than acting to discover clarity
emotions.south_asian_expression: often follows completing a family-prescribed path (a degree, a job) and finding no built-in next step of one's own.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम रास्ता नहीं खोज रहे — तुम इंतज़ार कर रहे हो कि कोई तुम्हें बता दे कि कौन सा रास्ता सही है।
pre_validation_line.en: You're not really searching for a direction. You're waiting for someone to confirm which one is the right one.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.3 - oil evaporates while water remains; those with clarity must act

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: अगर कोई गलत होने की संभावना ना हो, तो तुम अभी क्या करते?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: If there were no possibility of choosing wrong, what would you actually do right now?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never hand them a specific life plan — the teaching is about the courage to choose one's own dharma imperfectly, not about which path to pick.

emotions.name: Meaninglessness After Success
what_people_say: I got everything I wanted and I still feel empty
I thought this would fix how I feel, it didn't
I should be happy and I'm not, which makes it worse
Nothing I achieve actually satisfies me anymore
I'm successful by every external measure and still feel hollow
emotions.hidden_beneath: this is Arjuna's exact condition at the opening of the Gita — a person with everything, still collapsing. Not laziness, not ingratitude — a genuine confrontation with what actually matters.

patterns: achievement stated first, followed immediately by contradiction ('but')

emotions.likely_defence: guilt for feeling empty despite success, which delays actually examining the emptiness
emotions.south_asian_expression: extremely common after achieving the exact markers a family defined as success (the 'good job', the 'good marriage') with no roadmap for what comes after.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह वही जगह है जहां अर्जुन खड़ा था — सब कुछ पाकर भी, ठहर जाना।
pre_validation_line.en: This is exactly where Arjuna stood — everything within reach, and still, a complete stop.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.8 - a drop merging into the ocean, expansion not disappearance

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: जब तुमने यह हासिल किया, उस पल में क्या महसूस हुआ था — और अब क्या बदल गया है?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: In the actual moment you achieved this, what did it feel like — and what's shifted since?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never respond with 'be grateful for what you have' — this compounds the guilt rather than addressing the real philosophical gap.

emotions.name: Stagnation
what_people_say: I feel stuck, like nothing is moving forward
Every day feels the same
I know I need to change something but I don't
I've been saying I'll start for months
I feel like I'm watching my life from a standstill
emotions.hidden_beneath: safety found in the stillness, even though the person consciously wants movement

patterns: repetitive time language marking duration without change

emotions.likely_defence: stillness as unconscious protection from the risk of trying and failing
emotions.south_asian_expression: often masked as patience or waiting for the 'right time' sanctioned by family or tradition, when it is actually fear of the next uncertain step.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह ठहराव आलस्य नहीं है — यह किसी सुरक्षा की तलाश है, जो हिलने में नहीं मिलती।
pre_validation_line.en: This stillness isn't laziness. Some part of you finds safety here that movement threatens.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.3 - oil evaporates while water remains; those with clarity must act

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: अगर तुम हिले, तो सबसे बुरा क्या हो सकता है?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: If you actually moved, what's the worst thing that could realistically happen?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never say 'just start' without first exposing what the stillness is protecting against.

emotions.name: Existential Emptiness
what_people_say: I feel nothing, not even sad, just empty
I go through the motions without feeling anything
I used to feel things more, now it's just flat
I don't feel connected to anything anymore
Even the things I used to love don't reach me
emotions.hidden_beneath: protective numbness following prolonged unprocessed emotion — feeling nothing is easier than feeling everything at once

patterns: absence-of-feeling language, distinct from sadness — this is numbness, not grief

emotions.likely_defence: dissociation/numbing as accumulated protection
emotions.south_asian_expression: often follows years of suppressing emotion in service of duty — the suppression eventually generalises into full numbness.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह खालीपन शून्य नहीं है — यह वह जगह है जहां बहुत सारी भावनाएं इकट्ठा होकर बंद हो गई हैं।
pre_validation_line.en: This numbness isn't actually nothing. It's what happens when too much has been held for too long without release.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.9 - a lamp holding against deep darkness, however faint

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: क्या याद है, आखिरी बार जब तुमने वाकई कुछ गहराई से महसूस किया था?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Do you remember the last time you felt something deeply — what was happening then?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never try to force feeling back with intensity — approach this gently, the numbness is protective and needs to be respected before it's questioned.

emotions.name: Decision Paralysis
what_people_say: I've been going back and forth for months
I know what I should do but I can't move
Every option feels wrong
I keep waiting for more certainty before I decide
I feel frozen
emotions.hidden_beneath: fear of being wrong about oneself, disguised as fear of the wrong decision

patterns: oscillating structure — 'on one hand... on the other'

emotions.likely_defence: intellectualisation (endless analysis substituting for actual choice)
emotions.south_asian_expression: often layered with fear of disappointing family regardless of which option is chosen.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह दोनों रास्तों की बात नहीं है — यह डर है कि गलत चुनने का मतलब क्या निकलेगा तुम्हारे बारे में।
pre_validation_line.en: This isn't really about the two paths. It's about what choosing wrong would mean about you.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.1 - the closed fist versus the open palm

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: जब तुम चुनने की कोशिश करते हो, उस पल में असल में क्या रोकता है?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: In the actual moment you try to choose, what stops you?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never make the decision for them, and never say 'just pick one' without addressing the underlying fear first.

emotions.name: Overwhelm
what_people_say: There's too much, I can't cope
I don't know where to even start
Everything is happening at once
I feel like I'm drowning in responsibilities
I can't think clearly, there's too much noise in my head
emotions.hidden_beneath: volume that has exceeded actual capacity — not a character flaw, a genuine resource problem

patterns: list-like enumeration of stressors, run-on structure

emotions.likely_defence: none typically — usually a direct, honest report of genuine capacity overload
emotions.south_asian_expression: often includes invisible responsibilities (translating for parents, managing family logistics) not counted by the person as 'real' work, inflating the actual load beyond what's acknowledged.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह तुम्हारी कमी नहीं है — यह मात्रा तुम्हारी क्षमता से आगे निकल गई है।
pre_validation_line.en: This isn't a failure on your part. The amount has simply outpaced what any one person could hold.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.10 - patience, nothing blooms before its time

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: अगर तुम्हें सिर्फ एक चीज़ आज संभालनी हो, बाकी सब छोड़कर, वह क्या होगी?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: If you could handle just one thing today, and set the rest aside completely, what would it be?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never add more suggestions to an already overwhelmed person — reduce, don't expand, the field of what's in front of them.

emotions.name: Fear-Based Procrastination
what_people_say: I keep putting it off
I know I should start but I don't
I do everything except the one thing I actually need to do
I tell myself I'll start tomorrow
I don't understand why I can't just begin
emotions.hidden_beneath: fear disguised as laziness — starting risks confronting whether the fear was justified

patterns: displacement activity language — doing everything except the actual task

emotions.likely_defence: avoidance reframed as time-management failure rather than fear
emotions.south_asian_expression: frequently tied to high-stakes tasks with family expectation attached (applications, exams) where the fear of falling short of expectation is the real blocker.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह आलस्य नहीं है — तुम शुरू करने से नहीं डरते, तुम यह जानने से डरते हो कि शुरू करने के बाद क्या पता चलेगा।
pre_validation_line.en: This isn't laziness. You're not afraid of starting — you're afraid of what starting might reveal.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.3 - oil evaporates while water remains

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: अगर तुम अभी शुरू करो और यह ठीक ना गया, तो सबसे बुरा क्या साबित हो जाएगा?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: If you started this right now and it went badly, what would that actually prove?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never simply provide productivity tips — the block is emotional, not logistical.

emotions.name: Perfectionism-Induced Freeze
what_people_say: I can't submit this until it's perfect
I'd rather not show anyone than show something imperfect
I redo the same thing over and over
I know I'm overthinking this but I can't stop
If it's not the best, what's the point
emotions.hidden_beneath: the belief that imperfect output means the person themselves is not enough, not just the work

patterns: loop language — describing repeated, unfinished revision cycles

emotions.likely_defence: control over quality as a substitute for control over acceptance
emotions.south_asian_expression: often rooted in academic conditioning where less-than-top performance was treated as failure in itself.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह पूर्णता की चाह नहीं है — यह डर है कि अधूरा काम तुम्हें अधूरा साबित कर देगा।
pre_validation_line.en: This isn't really about wanting it perfect. It's the fear that anything less will prove something about you.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.1 - the closed fist versus the open palm

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: 'पूर्ण' किसने तय किया — और क्या वह मापदंड कभी हासिल होने वाला भी है?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Who set the definition of 'perfect' here — and is it actually reachable at all?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never say 'perfect is the enemy of good' as a bare cliché — connect it to the specific fear underneath, or it will bounce off.

emotions.name: Comparison-Induced Paralysis
what_people_say: Everyone my age seems ahead of me
I keep checking what other people are doing instead of doing my own thing
Social media makes me feel like I'm behind
I can't focus because I'm always comparing my progress to others
I don't even know if my goals are mine or just reactions to what others have
emotions.hidden_beneath: attention hijacked outward, away from one's own actual path, until the path itself becomes unclear

patterns: reference to others' progress embedded in nearly every sentence about self

emotions.likely_defence: using comparison as a proxy for self-evaluation, avoiding the harder work of internal assessment
emotions.south_asian_expression: intensified by direct, explicit family/community comparison culture — 'so-and-so's son/daughter' comparisons are often external and constant, not just internally generated.

pre_validation_line.hi: तुम्हारी नज़र इतनी देर से बाहर टिकी है कि तुम भूल गए हो कि तुम्हारा अपना रास्ता कैसा दिखता है।
pre_validation_line.en: Your attention has been fixed outward for so long that you've lost sight of what your own path even looks like.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.6 - the chain you bind yourself to shapes what you become

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: अगर तुम किसी को कभी ना देख पाते, तो तुम कहां होते अभी?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: If you could never see anyone else's progress at all, where would you actually be focusing right now?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never say 'stop comparing yourself to others' as flat advice — name the specific comparison happening and work from there.

emotions.name: General Burnout
what_people_say: I have nothing left to give
I'm running on empty
I can't remember the last time I felt rested
Everything feels like an effort now, even small things
I used to have energy for this, now I don't
emotions.hidden_beneath: complete resource depletion, often after sustained effort with insufficient restoration — not a motivation problem

patterns: depletion language, contrast with a previous energetic self

emotions.likely_defence: pushing through as identity (being seen as reliable/strong) rather than acknowledging depletion
emotions.south_asian_expression: often treated as weakness to admit within achievement-oriented family cultures — burnout gets reframed as 'just needing to try harder', deepening the depletion.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह तुम्हारी इच्छा की कमी नहीं है — यह वह सीमा है जहां शरीर और मन दोनों ने रुकने की मांग कर दी है।
pre_validation_line.en: This isn't a lack of will. This is the point where both body and mind have started demanding a stop.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.9 - a lamp needing oil, not just wanting to burn

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: आखिरी बार कब तुमने वाकई आराम किया था, बिना किसी अपराधबोध के?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: When did you last genuinely rest, without any guilt attached to it?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never suggest they simply 'push through' — burnout requires actual restoration, not more effort.

emotions.name: Chronic Exhaustion
what_people_say: I'm tired in a way that sleep doesn't fix
I wake up already exhausted
This isn't about needing a nap, it's deeper than that
My body is tired but so is something else in me
I don't know how much longer I can keep going like this
emotions.hidden_beneath: soul-level fatigue distinct from physical tiredness — meaning-depletion alongside energy-depletion

patterns: explicit distinction drawn between physical and non-physical tiredness

emotions.likely_defence: attributing everything to physical causes to avoid the deeper meaning-question underneath
emotions.south_asian_expression: the classic 'thaka hua' quality — a specific exhaustion that includes soul-tiredness, not just body-tiredness; this specific vocabulary should be honoured when it appears.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह 'थका हुआ' नींद से नहीं मिटेगा — यह उस थकान की बात है जो आत्मा तक पहुंच गई है।
pre_validation_line.en: This kind of tired doesn't resolve with sleep. This has reached somewhere sleep can't touch.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.9 - a lamp needing oil, not just wanting to burn

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: यह थकान शरीर की ज़्यादा है, या किसी और चीज़ की?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Is this exhaustion more in the body, or somewhere else entirely?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never respond only with practical rest suggestions — this is asking to be understood at a level deeper than logistics.

emotions.name: Compassion Fatigue
what_people_say: I've given everything to others and I'm empty
I don't have anything left for the people who need me
I feel guilty for being tired of caring
I used to feel more when people came to me with problems, now I feel numb to it
I'm the one everyone leans on and no one asks who holds me up
emotions.hidden_beneath: depletion specifically from sustained caregiving, layered with guilt about the depletion itself

patterns: caregiving-role language, contrast between past capacity and current numbness

emotions.likely_defence: guilt suppression of the fatigue to maintain the caregiver identity
emotions.south_asian_expression: extremely common for eldest children, especially daughters, who become the emotional infrastructure for extended family.

pre_validation_line.hi: जो थकान तुम महसूस कर रहे हो, वह देखभाल छोड़ने की इच्छा नहीं है — यह उस देखभाल का एक हिस्सा है जो अनदेखी रह गई।
pre_validation_line.en: This tiredness isn't a wish to stop caring. It's what happens when the caring itself goes unheld.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.3 - oil evaporates while water remains, both are needed

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: आखिरी बार कब किसी ने तुमसे पूछा था कि तुम्हें क्या चाहिए?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: When did someone last ask you what you needed?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never suggest they simply 'care less' — reframe toward sustainable giving, not withdrawal of care.

emotions.name: Disillusionment
what_people_say: I worked so hard for this and it wasn't worth it
I believed in something and it let me down
I don't trust the process anymore
I feel foolish for having hoped this much
Nothing turned out the way I was told it would
emotions.hidden_beneath: grief for a belief system (about effort, fairness, or a specific path) that has been contradicted by lived experience

patterns: before/after belief structure — what was believed vs. what actually happened

emotions.likely_defence: cynicism as protection against future hope and further disappointment
emotions.south_asian_expression: often tied to the specific promise that following a prescribed path (education, career) guarantees a specific outcome — disillusionment hits hardest when that implicit contract is broken.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह सिर्फ नतीजे का दुख नहीं है — यह उस विश्वास के टूटने का दुख है जिस पर तुमने सब कुछ टिका दिया था।
pre_validation_line.en: This isn't only grief for the outcome. It's grief for the belief you built everything on top of.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.4 - the sky dirty before rain, clean after

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: किस पर विश्वास टूटा है — खुद पर, दूसरों पर, या इस विचार पर कि मेहनत हमेशा फल देती है?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: What actually broke here — trust in yourself, in others, or in the idea that effort always pays off?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never simply promise 'it will work out next time' — this repeats the exact pattern that led to the disillusionment.

emotions.name: Protective Numbness
what_people_say: I can't feel anything anymore
I know I should be upset but I just feel flat
I've stopped reacting to things that used to affect me
I feel disconnected from my own life
Even good news doesn't really reach me
emotions.hidden_beneath: a genuine protective shutdown after too much has been held for too long — not coldness, but overload

patterns: absence-of-response language across both positive and negative events

emotions.likely_defence: dissociation as the nervous system's own protective response
emotions.south_asian_expression: commonly follows years of required emotional suppression in service of family harmony or duty; the shutdown is often a learned survival skill, not a personal failing.

pre_validation_line.hi: यह भावहीनता निर्दयता नहीं है — यह वह जगह है जहां बहुत कुछ महसूस करना असंभव हो गया, इसलिए मन ने बंद कर दिया।
pre_validation_line.en: This flatness isn't coldness. It's what happens when there was too much to feel, so something in you turned the volume down.

emotions.metaphor_ref: 4.9 - a lamp holding against deep darkness, however faint

opening_diagnostic_question.hi: क्या याद है, जब यह भावहीनता पहली बार शुरू हुई थी?
opening_diagnostic_question.en: Do you remember roughly when this numbness first began?

emotions.never_for_this_emotion: Never try to force emotional intensity as a fix — approach gently; the numbness served a protective purpose and deserves respect before it's questioned.
